consensus_summary: A committed learner-follower/apprentice of Jesus (essentially every Christian), marked by obedience, self-denial, cross-bearing, imitation, abiding in his word, love, and fruit-bearing; majority view equates disciple with believer while noting narrower historical (the Twelve) and minority two-tier usages.
book_summary: One in whom the law is sealed (Isa 8:16), proven by continuing in the word, love, and fruit; who meets Jesus’ thrice-stated conditions of leaving all, bearing the cross, and forsaking possessions; baptized into the Name and perfected as his master—the Head whose Name carries the Word, covenant law, and fruitful priesthood.
book_core_identification: one in whom the law is sealed (true covenant bearer under the Name)
boundary_disagreement: Book treats sealing of the law plus absolute renunciation (Luke 14’s three ‘cannot be my disciple’) as definitional boundaries and adds Name/baptism/priesthood layers, excluding or reclassifying nominal or less-committed believers whom majority consensus includes via Acts usage and the Great Commission.
material_contradiction: None; the book retains and cites the same NT marks (continue in word, love, fruit, cross, cost) as proofs rather than denying them.
rationale: Cores share the same general referent (Jesus’ disciples) and the book explicitly notes the common learner-follower view, yet it materially refines identification, conditions, and precision around Isa 8:16 sealing, New-Covenant law-writing, divine Name, and perfection-as-master, thereby narrowing the extension without replacing the category.
strongest_objection: Isaiah 8:16 and the OT Name/law texts do not redefine NT discipleship; Acts usage and the Great Commission treat ‘disciple’ as coextensive with all believers, so the sealing-plus-absolute-cost boundary and priestly Name symbolism are an unrequired narrowing and over-reading.
